  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3143307" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c142387561" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Use of Estimates</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The preparation of the consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates, assumptions and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the period. Significant estimates for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025,&#160;</em>include the (i) valuation of the liability classified warrants,&#160;(ii)&#160;unbilled clinical trial costs, and (iii) stock-based compensation expense. Although actual results could differ from those estimates, such estimates are developed based on the best information available to management and management&#8217;s best judgments at the time.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387562" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Cash and cash equivalents</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company considers all highly liquid investments with an original maturity of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less to be cash equivalents. The Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142384215"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142384649">not</span></span> have any cash equivalents as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk" id="c142387563" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Concentrations of credit risk</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to a significant concentration of credit risk consist primarily of cash. Periodically, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>maintain deposits in financial institutions in excess of government insured limits. Any loss incurred or a lack of access to such funds could have a significant adverse impact on the Company&#8217;s financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:TradeAndOtherAccountsReceivablePolicy" id="c142387564" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Accounts Receivable</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company recognizes accounts receivables from sales to customers at the time revenue is recognized&#160;and a customer invoice is created.&#160;The need for a credit loss allowance is evaluated each reporting period based on the Company&#8217;s assessment of the credit worthiness of its customers or any other potential circumstances that could result in a credit loss. The Company initially estimates credit losses based on a portfolio-wide method using an aging schedule at the end of each reporting period. Any customer specific collections subsequent to the reporting period are then adjusted accordingly. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the Company had a current expected credit loss reserve of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384218" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivableCurrent" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3</ix:nonFraction> thousand and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384219" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivableCurrent" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387565" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Income taxes</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company recognizes deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been included in the consolidated financial statements or tax returns. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on the difference between the consolidated financial statement carrying amounts and the tax bases of assets and liabilities using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the periods in which such differences are expected to reverse. A valuation allowance is provided when the realization of net deferred tax assets is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deemed more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

      <div class="hf-cell" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin: 0pt; width: calc(100% - 1px); display: inline-block;">

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company complies with the provisions of Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> <i>Income Taxes</i>, which provides a comprehensive model for the recognition, measurement, and disclosure in consolidated financial statements of uncertain income tax positions that a company has taken or expects to take on a tax return. Under this guidance, a company can recognize the benefit of an income tax position only if it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> (greater than <em style="font: inherit;">50%</em>) that the tax position will be sustained upon tax examination, based solely on the technical merits of the tax position; otherwise, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> benefit can be recognized. The tax benefits recognized are measured based on the largest benefit that has a greater than <em style="font: inherit;">50%</em> likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement. Additionally, the Company accrues interest and related penalties, if applicable, on all tax exposures for which reserves have been established consistent with jurisdictional tax laws. Interest and penalties are classified as income tax expense in the consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387566" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Use of Derivative Instruments</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company&#8217;s derivative instruments historically have consisted of financial instruments that arose as part of the Company&#8217;s ongoing efforts to raise capital to fund the Company&#8217;s operations. It is likely that ongoing efforts to raise capital in the future will result in additional derivative instruments to be issued as part of those efforts. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> nor does it intend to utilize derivative instruments for risk management (i.e. hedging) or investing activities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">These derivative instruments have taken the form of warrants, convertible debt, and other financing arrangements such as a prepaid forward purchase option. The classification of these financial instruments as either a component of liabilities or equity is specific to the terms within each financial instrument agreement. and the application of U.S. GAAP. For those that are liability classified, the Company recognized changes in the fair value of each financial instruments as a &#8220;non-operating income / (expense)&#8221; component of the consolidated statement of operations and an adjustment to operating cash flows within the consolidated statement of cash flows each reporting period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The issuance of each derivative instrument is reported as a proceed in the financing section to the consolidated statement of cash flows, while the ultimate settlement of each derivative instrument could be reported either as an adjustment to operating cash flows, paydown within financing cash flows, or a non-cash transaction depending on the settlement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387567" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Fair value option of accounting</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">Generally, when financial instruments are <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> acquired that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to be recorded at fair value per U.S. GAAP, ASC <em style="font: inherit;">825,</em> <i>Financial Instruments</i> allows an entity to elect the fair value option (&#8220;FVO&#8221;). The FVO <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be elected on an instrument-by-instrument basis only at the time of acquisition and once elected is irrevocable. The FVO allows an entity to account for the entire financial instrument at fair value with subsequent changes in fair value recognized in earnings through the consolidated statements of operations at each reporting date. A financial instrument is generally eligible for the FVO if, amongst other factors, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> part of the financial instrument is classified in stockholders&#8217; equity.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">Based on the eligibility assessment discussed above, the Company historically concluded that its previously held&#160;convertible notes&#160;were eligible for the FVO and accordingly elected the FVO for those debt instruments. This election was made because of operational efficiencies in valuing and reporting for these debt instruments at fair value in their entirety at each reporting date. The convertible notes contained certain embedded derivatives that otherwise would require bifurcation and separate accounting at fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The convertible notes, inclusive of their respective accrued interest at the stated interest rates (collectively referred to as the &#8220;FVO debt instruments&#8221;) were initially recorded at fair value as liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets and subsequently re-measured at fair value at the end of each reporting period presented within the consolidated financial statements until they were settled in <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em> The changes in fair value of the FVO debt instruments are recorded in changes in fair value of convertible notes, included as a component of other income (expense), net, in the consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have any convertible notes outstanding&#160;during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy" id="c142387568" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Fair value of financial instruments</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The following provides a summary of those assets or liabilities for which the Company is required to measure at fair value either on a recurring basis, the valuation techniques and summary of inputs used to arrive at the measure of fair value. Changes in fair value of these assets or liabilities are recognized as a component of net income in the consolidated statements of operations. Changes in fair value of these assets or liabilities are considered unrealized gains or losses and therefore are classified as non-cash adjustments to reconcile net income to operating cash flows. Significant increases (decreases) in unobservable inputs used in fair value measurements could, in isolation, potentially result in a significantly lower or higher valuation for those assets or liabilities requiring recurring fair value measurements at each reporting date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;"><i>Liability Classified Warrants.</i> The Company has entered into or assumed various financial instruments, in the form of warrant agreements, that require classification as liabilities. This classification requires that the Company measure the warrants at each fair value at the end of each quarterly and annual&#160;reporting period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company uses a Black-Scholes option pricing model to fair value the warrants, using standard option pricing inputs such as the strike price of each warrant tranche, estimated volatility, time to maturity, and the risk-free interest rate. The risk-free interest rate is the U.S. Treasury rate at the date of issuance, and the time to maturity is based on the contractual life at the date of issuance, which is <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> years. The change in fair value of the liability classified warrants each reporting period is recorded to the change in fair value of warrants liability in the consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;"><i>Operating Current Assets and Current Liabilities. </i>The estimated fair value of cash, accounts receivables, prepaid expenses, accounts payable and accrued expenses approximate their fair value because of the short-term nature of these instruments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;"><i>Classification of Derivative Gains and Losses on the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows. </i>Changes in fair value related to the Company&#8217;s derivative financial instruments consisting of (i) liability classified warrants and&#160;(ii) convertible notes&#160;are classified in operating cash flows as adjustments to net income. During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the only activity related to liability classified warrants, as the Company fully settled all outstanding convertible notes during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387569" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Revenue Recognition </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Overall</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">Under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> the Company recognizes revenue when a customer obtains control of promised goods or services, in an amount that reflects the consideration that the Company expects to receive in exchange for those goods or services. To determine revenue recognition for arrangements that the Company determines are within the scope of Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> the Company evaluates the following criteria: (i) identify the contract with a customer; (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract; (iii) determine the transaction price, including variable consideration, if any; (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">At contract inception, once the contract is determined to be within the scope of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> the Company assesses whether the goods or services promised within each contract are distinct and, therefore, represent a separate performance obligation. Goods and services that are determined <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be distinct are combined with other promised goods and services until a distinct combined performance obligation is identified. The Company then allocates the transaction price to each performance obligation and recognizes the associated revenue when (or as) each performance obligation is satisfied. The estimate of the transaction price for each contract includes all variable consideration to which the Company expects to be entitled, subject to the constraint on variable consideration. The Company constrains revenue by giving consideration to factors that could otherwise lead to a probable reversal of revenue. Variable consideration is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> constrained if the potential reversal of cumulative revenue recognized at the contract level is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> significant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company records any payments received from customers prior to the Company fulfilling its performance obligation(s) as contract obligations. Amounts expected to be recognized as revenue within the <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year following the consolidated balance sheet date are classified as current contract obligations. Amounts <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to be recognized as revenue within the <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year following the consolidated balance sheet date are classified as contract obligations, net of current portion. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8211; Revenues and Contract Obligations for further details.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Product Sales Revenue</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company has sold and intends to continue to sell its products either through a combination of distributor(s) and/or directly to end-user qualified customers through the Company&#8217;s own internal commercial/sales resources. The acting distributor during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024 </em>subsequently resold and was to continue to resell the products to present and future customers, until such time the Company terminated its agreement with the distributor (see Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>).</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CostOfSalesPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387570" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Cost of Goods Sold</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:23pt;">Prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2024, </em>the Company manufactured/assembled QUELIMMUNE and adult SCDs only for research oriented and/or clinical trial related activities. Inventory purchased prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2024 </em>was expensed as a period expense at the time of purchase as a research and development expense. Accordingly, all QUELIMMUNE units sold prior to the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025, </em>had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> recognized inventory value. During the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company recognized approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384258" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">53</ix:nonFraction> thousand for cost of goods sold.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:23pt;">The Company purchases supplies for the production of QUELIMMUNE and adult SCDs, some of which is used in the production of both. The Company's policy for the accounting for these <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> categories of inventory as follows:&#160;</p>

<tr><td style="width: 45px;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 21px; vertical-align: top;">&#8226;</td><td style="width: 1068px;"><i>Commingled Inventory&#160;&#8211;&#160;</i>comprises raw materials that are used both for the assembly of QUELIMMUNE or adult SCDs.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c142387571" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Stock-based compensation</i></b><i> </i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">In accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">718,</em> <i>Compensation </i>&#8211;<i> Stock Compensation</i>, the Company recognizes compensation expense for all stock-based awards issued to employees based on the estimated grant-date fair value, which is recognized as expense on a graded vesting approach over the requisite service period. The Company has elected to recognize forfeitures as they occur. The fair value of stock options is determined using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. The determination of fair value for stock options on the date of grant using an option-pricing model requires management to make certain assumptions including implied volatility, expected term, risk-free interest rate and expected dividends (<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142384261">$nil</span>) in addition to the Company&#8217;s common stock valuation. The determination of fair value of restricted stock units is valued based on the value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the grant date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpensePolicy" id="c142387574" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Research and development expenses </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">Expenditures made for research and development are charged to expense as incurred. External costs consist primarily of payments for laboratory supplies purchased in connection with the Company&#8217;s discovery and preclinical activities, and process development and clinical development activities. Internal costs consist primarily of employee-related costs, consultants fees and costs related to compliance with regulatory requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company records expenses related to external research and development services based on services received and efforts expended pursuant to invoices and contracts with consultants that supply, conduct, and manage preclinical studies and clinical trials on its behalf.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">&#160;</p><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i>Funded Research &amp; Development Expense</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt;">During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company entered into an agreement to provide contract research services to an outside party, which involves a study of the Company's selective cytopheretic device relating to patients with severe, chronic heart failure. The Company is able to bill the outside party for a certain portion of the costs incurred to provide these services. The Company will own and is able to benefit from the knowledge gained from the results of this study. Accordingly, the Company will account for any funds paid by the outside party to the Company as a reimbursed expense, in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">730</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em> as a funded research and development arrangement. Accordingly, any amounts incurred and billed will offset the Company's operating expenses categorized as research and development expense on the Company&#8217;s condensed consolidated statement of operations for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025. </em>The reimbursed expenses for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>totaled approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384264" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="icu:FundedResearchAndDevelopmentReimbursedExpenses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> funded research and development agreement existed in <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="icu:EmergingGrowthCompanyStatusPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387575" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Emerging growth company status</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company is an &#8220;emerging growth company&#8221;, as defined in the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of <em style="font: inherit;">2012</em> (&#8220;JOBS Act&#8221;). Under the JOBS Act, emerging growth companies can take advantage of an extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards, delaying the adoption of these accounting standards until they would apply to private companies. The Company has elected to use this extended transition period for complying with certain new or revised accounting standards that have different effective dates for public and private companies until the earlier of the date that it is (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer an emerging growth company or (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) affirmatively and irrevocably opt out of the extended transition period provided in the JOBS Act.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c142387576" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Net loss per share attributable to common stockholders</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company&#8217;s basic net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is calculated by dividing the net loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding for the period. The diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is computed by giving effect to all potential dilutive common stock equivalents outstanding for the period. The dilutive effect of these potential common shares is reflected in diluted earnings per share by application of the treasury stock method. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">14</em>&#160;for disclosures on exclusion of certain instruments which would be anti-dilutive in circumstances where the Company is reporting a net loss for that earnings period. Basic and diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is presented in conformity with the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method required for participating securities as certain outstanding warrants are considered participating securities. The Company&#8217;s participating securities do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a contractual obligation to share in the Company&#8217;s losses. As such, the net loss was attributed entirely to common stockholders. As the Company has reported a net loss for the periods presented, diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is the same as basic net loss per share attributable to common stockholders for these periods.&#160;The significant increase in common stock outstanding is expected to impact the year-over-year comparability of the Company&#8217;s net loss per share calculations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142387578" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Recently adopted accounting standards</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Accounting Standards Update <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> </i>&#8212;<i> </i>In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> <i>Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>) Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</i>. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> enhances the transparency and decision usefulness of income tax disclosures. The amendments in this update are effective for public business entities for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024. </em>Early adoption was permitted, but the Company elected <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to early adopt and adopted for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025. </em>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> requires&#160;the Company to consistently categorize and provide greater disaggregation of information in the rate reconciliation it must further disaggregate income taxes paid. However, as the Company is currently generating net operating losses, pays <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> federal and limited state taxes and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> operate in foreign jurisdictions, this does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a significant impact to the Company's income tax disclosures (see Note <em style="font: inherit;">13</em>).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Recently issued accounting standards <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet adopted </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;"><i>Accounting Standards Update <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> </i>&#8212;<i> </i>In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> - <i>Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income </i>&#8211;<i> Expense Disaggregation (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> requires the disclosure of additional information related to certain costs and expenses, including amounts of inventory purchases, employee compensation, and depreciation and amortization included in each income statement line item. The ASU is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting this guidance on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> Revenues and Contract Obligations</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2022, </em>the Company entered into a License and Distribution Agreement (the &#8220;Distribution Agreement&#8221;) with Nuwellis, Inc. (&#8220;Nuwellis&#8221;) granting exclusive distribution rights of the Company&#8217;s pediatric SCD within the United States of America. Under the terms of the Distribution Agreement, Nuwellis would pay the Company consideration comprising both (i) a per unit sales price for each unit shipped and (ii) a royalty for all units sold to customers.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">In addition, Nuwellis also agreed to pay (i) a $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384300" contextRef="d_2022-12-01_2022-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:ProceedsFromUpfrontLicensingPayment" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">100</ix:nonFraction> thousand upfront payment at contract inception (the &#8220;Up-front Payment&#8221;), and (ii) <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> contingent milestones payments consisting of (a) $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384302" contextRef="d_2022-12-01_2022-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_StatementScenarioAxis-RegulatoryMilestoneMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:MilestonePayments" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">450</ix:nonFraction> thousand payment upon meeting the regulatory milestone of receiving HDE approval from the FDA (the &#8220;Regulatory Milestone Payment&#8221;), and (b) $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384303" contextRef="d_2022-12-01_2022-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_StatementScenarioAxis-SalesBasedMilestoneMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:MilestonePayments" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">300</ix:nonFraction> thousand payment upon meeting a sales-based milestone (the &#8220;Sales Based Milestone Payment&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company had the following performance obligations within the Distribution Agreement: (i) a material right to Nuwellis consisting of an exclusive option for Nuwellis to purchase additional pediatric SCDs during the term of the Distribution Agreement for a discounted price, (ii) to provide training to Nuwellis personnel and medical professionals at end-user customers of Nuwellis and (iii) upon each receipt of a valid Nuwellis purchase order, delivery of pediatric SCDs. The transaction price for the Nuwellis material right and training is comprised of the Upfront Payment, the Regulatory Milestone Payment and the Sales Based Milestone Payment. The transaction price for each pediatric SCD device sold was the actual price for each device and the estimated royalties to be received.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">Prior to the Company&#8217;s termination of the Distribution Agreement discussed below, the Company received full consideration for the Up-front Payment and the Regulatory Milestone Payment for a total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384304" contextRef="d_2022-12-01_2022-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityConsiderationReceived" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">550</ix:nonFraction> thousand, which had been recorded as contract liabilities and was to be recognized over the remaining term of the Distribution Agreement. However, the Company and Nuwellis entered into a confidential settlement agreement on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 20, 2024 (</em>the &#8220;Settlement Agreement&#8221;), in connection with the Company&#8217;s termination of the Distribution Agreement on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 18, 2024. </em>Under the Settlement Agreement the Company agreed to refund Nuwellis the entire $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384305" contextRef="d_2024-10-20_2024-10-20_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityConsiderationReceived" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">550</ix:nonFraction> thousand comprising of the Upfront Payment and Regulatory Milestone plus an additional $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384306" contextRef="d_2024-10-20_2024-10-20_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:ContractWithCustomerRefundLiabilityAdditionalReturn" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">350</ix:nonFraction> thousand for a total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384307" contextRef="i_2024-10-20_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerRefundLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">900</ix:nonFraction> thousand, of which the $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384308" contextRef="d_2024-10-20_2024-10-20_CounterpartyNameAxis-NuwellisMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:ContractWithCustomerRefundLiabilityAdditionalReturn" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">350</ix:nonFraction> thousand was charged to general and administrative expense. The amounts were paid to Nuwellis in <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> installments during the quarter ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">As a result, the Company (i) was precluded from recognizing revenue of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384310" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_ProductOrServiceAxis-PediatricScdsMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAndDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:UnrecognizableRevenue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million for product shipments to Nuwellis during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, (</em>ii) was precluded from recognizing any revenues related to contract liabilities arising the Upfront Payment and Regulatory Milestone through <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, (</em>see below), and (iii) does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate there will be any future shipments of pediatric SCDs to Nuwellis going forward. Due to the termination of the Distribution Agreement and related Settlement Agreement, the Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize any revenue from the Up-Front Payment or the Regulatory Milestone Payment as it refunded the payments to Nuwellis as part of the Settlement Agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">Since the termination of the Distribution Agreement, the Company developed its own commercial operations and sold approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384313" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ProductOrServiceAxis-PediatricScdsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384314" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_ProductOrServiceAxis-PediatricScdsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million to end-user customers during the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The following table summarizes the changes in the Company&#8217;s contract liability balance for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>:</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Insurance Financing</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2025, &#65279; </em>the Company entered into a financing arrangement with a lender to finance a portion of the annual premium of an insurance policy in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384326" contextRef="i_2025-10-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-FinancingOfInsurancePolicyPremiumsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million. Interest on the financing agreement was <ix:nonFraction id="c142384327" contextRef="i_2025-10-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-FinancingOfInsurancePolicyPremiumsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">7.940</ix:nonFraction>% per annum. The <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2025 </em>financing agreement is to be paid in <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> monthly installments, with the final installment set for <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2024, </em>the Company entered into a financing arrangement with a lender to finance a portion of the annual premium of an insurance policy in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384329" contextRef="i_2024-10-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-FinancingOfInsurancePolicyPremiumsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million. Interest on the financing agreement was <ix:nonFraction id="c142384330" contextRef="i_2024-10-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-FinancingOfInsurancePolicyPremiumsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">8.440</ix:nonFraction>% per annum. The <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2024 </em>financing agreement was to be paid in <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> monthly installments, but was paid in full in <em style="font: inherit;"> June 2025.&#160;&#160;</em></p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 23pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>Common Warrants became exercisable on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 28, 2025, </em>the effective date of stockholder approval for the issuance of the shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of the warrants and expire on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 28, 2030.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 23pt;">Prior to their exercise, the <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>Pre-Funded Warrants had dividend participation rights, and any unexercised pre-funded warrants are included in the Company's weighted-average shares outstanding for calculation of the Company's net loss per share.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 23pt;">In connection with the <em style="font: inherit;"> February&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Offering, the Company amended the exercise price of the <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2024 </em>Series A and <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2024 </em>Series B Common Warrants (collectively the <em style="font: inherit;"> &#8220;January 2024 </em>Warrants&#8221;), issued in a previous financing transaction with the same institutional investor in <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2024, </em>to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384406" contextRef="i_2024-01-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-January2024WarrantsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">17.00</ix:nonFraction>&#160;from the original exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384407" contextRef="i_2025-02-03_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-January2024WarrantsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">207.60</ix:nonFraction>. Furthermore, the expiration date of all <ix:nonFraction id="c142384408" contextRef="i_2025-02-28_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-January2024WarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">65,046</ix:nonFraction>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2024 </em>Warrants was extended to <em style="font: inherit;"> January 30, 2029, </em>upon stockholder approval on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 28, 2025. </em><em style="font: inherit;">No</em> <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2024 </em>Warrants have been exercised and all <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2024 </em>Warrants remain outstanding as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 23pt;">The Company&#160;issued <ix:nonFraction id="c142384410" contextRef="i_2025-02-03_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-February2025PlacementAgentWarrantsMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-Q12025SecuritiesPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">24,706</ix:nonFraction>&#160;warrants to its placement agent (the <em style="font: inherit;"> "February 2025 </em>PA Warrants") to purchase shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384411" contextRef="i_2025-02-03_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-February2025PlacementAgentWarrantsMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-Q12025SecuritiesPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">21.25</ix:nonFraction>. The <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>PA Warrants were exercisable upon issuance and expire on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 30, 2029. </em>The <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>PA Warrants and <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>Common Warrants are herein defined as the <em style="font: inherit;"> "February 2025 </em>Warrants".&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No</em> <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>Warrants have been exercised and all <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>Warrants remain outstanding as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 23pt;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40,</em> <i>Derivatives and Hedging-Contracts in Entity</i>&#8217;<i>s own Equity</i>, the Company determined that all the different warrants issued or amended in connection with the <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2025 </em>Offering met the conditions for equity classification and were included as a component of stockholders&#8217; equity/(deficit).</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i>At-The-Market Offering</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 23pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 20, 2024, </em>the Company entered into an At-The-Market Offering Agreement (the &#8220;ATM Agreement&#8221;) with Wainwright as sales agent, to sell shares of its common stock, from time to time, through an &#8220;at the market offering&#8221; program under which Wainwright will act as sales agent. The sales, if any, of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock made under the ATM Agreement will be made by any method permitted by law deemed to be an &#8220;at the market offering&#8221; as defined in Rule <em style="font: inherit;">415</em> promulgated under the Securities Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1933,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;), including sales made directly on or through the Nasdaq Capital Market or on any other existing trading market for the Company&#8217;s common stock (the &#8220;ATM&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 23pt;">Through <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company has raised approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384417" contextRef="d_2024-08-21_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtthemarketAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStock" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10.4</ix:nonFraction> million, net of offering costs of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384418" contextRef="d_2024-08-21_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtthemarketAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:EquityOfferingIssuanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million utilizing the ATM since inception in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2024, </em>issuing approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142384419" contextRef="d_2024-08-21_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtthemarketAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million shares of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock. During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company raised approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384420" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtthemarketAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStock" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.9</ix:nonFraction> million, net of offering costs of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384421" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtthemarketAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfStockIssuanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million, issuing approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142384422" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtthemarketAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.9</ix:nonFraction> million shares of the Company's common stock.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -28pt; text-indent: 23pt;"><b><i>Standby Equity Purchase Agreement </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -28pt; text-indent: 50pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 26pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 25, 2025, </em>the Company entered into a standby equity purchase agreement (&#8220;Common Stock Purchase Agreement&#8221;) and related registration rights agreement (the &#8220;Registration Rights Agreement&#8221;) with Lincoln Park Capital Fund, LLC (&#8220;Lincoln Park&#8221;), collectively the &#8220;SEPA&#8221;. Pursuant to the Common Stock Purchase Agreement, the Company has the right, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the obligation, to direct Lincoln Park to purchase up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384425" contextRef="d_2025-04-25_2025-04-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-LincolnParkCapitalFundLlcMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-StandbyEquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="icu:ShareIssuableMaximumValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">15.0</ix:nonFraction> million in aggregate gross purchase price of newly issued shares of Common Stock, subject to certain limitations and conditions as described below (the &#8220;SEPA Program&#8221;) at a purchase price equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c142384426" contextRef="i_2025-04-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-LincolnParkCapitalFundLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-StandbyEquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="icu:ShareIssuedPricePerSharePercentageOfSalePrice" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">97</ix:nonFraction>% of the lesser of (i) the lowest sale price of the common stock on the purchase date or (ii) average of the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> lowest closing sale prices of the common stock over the last <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em> business days prior to the purchase date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 26pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 26pt; text-align: justify;">The Company controls the timing and amount of any sales to Lincoln Park, which depend on a variety of factors including, among other things, market conditions, the trading price of the Company&#8217;s common stock, and determinations by the Company as to appropriate sources of funding for its business and operations. However, Lincoln Park&#8217;s obligation to purchase shares is subject to certain conditions, including the daily trading volume of the Company&#8217;s stock. In all instances, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> sell shares of Common Stock under the Purchase Agreement if it would result in Lincoln Park and its affiliate beneficially owning more than <ix:nonFraction id="c142384430" contextRef="i_2025-04-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-LincolnParkCapitalFundLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-StandbyEquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="icu:OwnershipOfOutstandingVotingPowerPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">9.99</ix:nonFraction>% of outstanding voting power or shares of the Common Stock at any <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> point in time.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 26pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 26pt; text-align: justify;">As part of the SEPA, the Company agreed to pay Lincoln Park <ix:nonFraction id="c142384432" contextRef="d_2025-04-25_2025-04-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-LincolnParkCapitalFundLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-StandbyEquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">23,641</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, valued at approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384433" contextRef="d_2025-04-25_2025-04-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-LincolnParkCapitalFundLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-StandbyEquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueNewIssues" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million on the date of issuance, <em style="font: inherit;"> April 25, 2025 (</em>the &#8220;Commitment Fee&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 26pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 26pt; text-align: justify;">The Company evaluated the contract that includes the right to require Lincoln Park to purchase shares of common stock in the future (&#8220;put right&#8221;) considering the guidance in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40,</em> <i>Derivatives and Hedging </i>&#8212;<i> Contracts on an Entity</i>&#8217;<i>s Own Equity</i> and concluded that it is an equity-linked contract that does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> qualify for equity classification, and therefore requires fair value accounting. The Company analyzed the terms of the freestanding put right and concluded that it has an immaterial value at the issuance date of <em style="font: inherit;"> April 25, 2025, </em>and&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 25pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Through <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company raised approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142384437" contextRef="d_2025-04-25_2025-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-LincolnParkCapitalFundLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-StandbyEquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOrSaleOfEquity" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">40</ix:nonFraction> thousand and issued <ix:nonFraction id="c142384438" contextRef="d_2025-04-25_2025-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-LincolnParkCapitalFundLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-StandbyEquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company's common stock.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">9.</em> Common Stock and Preferred Stock</b></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:29pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company is authorized to issue <ix:nonFraction id="c142384446" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="icu:TotalSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">460,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares, consisting of (a) <ix:nonFraction id="c142384447" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">450,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock and (b) <ix:nonFraction id="c142384448" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of preferred stock (the &#8220;Preferred Stock&#8221;). On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 18, 2025, </em>the Company&#8217;s shareholders voted at a Special Meeting to reduce the authorized shares of common stock to <ix:nonFraction id="c142384449" contextRef="i_2026-01-05_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">425,000,000</ix:nonFraction>.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Voting power</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:29pt;">Except as otherwise required by law or as otherwise provided in any certificate of designation for any series of preferred stock, the holders of common stock possess all voting power for the election of the Company&#8217;s directors and all other matters requiring stockholder action. Holders of common stock are entitled to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> voter per share on matters to be voted on by stockholders. The Charter does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> provide for cumulative voting rights.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Dividends</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:29pt;">Subject to the rights, if any, of the holders of any outstanding shares of preferred stock, under the Charter, holders of common stock will be entitled to receive such dividends, if any, as <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be declared from time to time by the Board of Directors in its discretion out of funds legally available therefor.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Liquidation, dissolution and winding-up</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:29pt;">In the event of the Company&#8217;s voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution, distribution of assets or winding-up, the holders of the common stock will be entitled to receive an equal amount per share of all of the Company&#8217;s assets of whatever kind available for distribution to stockholders after the rights of the holders of the Preferred Stock have been satisfied and after payment or provision for payment of the Company&#8217;s debts.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Preemptive or other rights</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:29pt;">There are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> preemptive rights or sinking fund provisions applicable to the shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Preferred stock</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:29pt;">The Charter provides that shares of preferred stock <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued from time to time in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more series. The Board of Directors is authorized to fix the voting rights, if any, designations, powers, preferences, the relative, participating, optional, or other special rights and any qualifications, limitations, and restrictions thereof, applicable to the shares of each series. The Company has <ix:nonFraction id="c142384455" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockSharesOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> preferred stock outstanding at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> or <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Equity incentive plan - summary</i></b></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Omnibus Incentive Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:28pt;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors adopted, and the shareholders approved the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Omnibus Incentive Plan to provide long-term incentive for its employees and non-employee service providers. The vesting of stock options is stated in each individual grant agreement, which is generally either <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142384461">one</span> or <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142384462">four</span> years. Options granted expire <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022OmnibusEquityIncentivePlanMember" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" id="c142384463" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years after the date of grant.</p>
